hook_text: Every day, buses pull into Park Station full of people who have just left home for good. Why?
clip_script: Back home: no jobs, a plot too small to feed everyone, a drought that killed the cattle, a clinic two hours' walk away. Those are push factors. In the city: the hope of a job, better pay, a college, a hospital, electricity, and a cousin who says there is work in construction. Those are pull factors. Put them on a scale. When the push and the pull outweigh the cost of the journey, people move. Millions do it every year across Africa, the fastest-urbanising continent on earth. In South Africa, about two in three people already live in towns and cities, and one in four lives in tiny Gauteng.
visual_style: A whiteboard balance scale with rural push icons on one side and city pull icons on the other, a bus moving from a village to a skyline, and a map of Africa with growing city dots.
pacing: Quick lists of push and pull, then a steady close.
